detail.longDescription: My home automations know thresholds, not context. Sump pump runs 2 min after a rainy night → alert. Long shower → "possible leak". Washer pauses to soak → "finished", 20 min too early. So I gave the "is this normal?" question to Jev, TypeSafe's decision model. You send it a few lines of facts and a typed question, and it answers with a calibrated probability. No free text, no JSON to parse. How it's wired into Home Assistant: • The old rule always computes its answer. Jev only advises. • One switch: shadow (log only), active, or off. • An error, a spent budget or low confidence → the rule wins, so the alert still fires. • 6 automations: sump pump, water, temperature drops, shutters, ventilation, laundry. Cost: 133 calls and 75k tokens on day one, about $3 a year for the whole house. Two lessons that aren't about AI: 1. Writing the facts for the model made me read them. Two humidity sensors had been stuck at 0 %, and my old rules were using them. 2. My GitOps sync had been failing silently for 5 weeks. Merged ≠ deployed. Also in the post: can Laya do the same job locally, to keep occupancy data at home? https:// blog.mornati.net/jev-home-assi stant-letting-a-decision-model-judge-my-automations/ # HomeAssistant # SmartHome # HomeAutomation # LLM # AI # SelfHosted
